about: Owner's progression plan (2026-10-23 19:27 / 19:36): targets vs today, by advancement, leftover mistakes, eggs and babies, Map 0-1 skills, Ants, faction pacing, collection by map. Nothing in the game was changed.

mistakes.what: The three packs share one pool: Hedgerow Pouch (Pack 1), Tidemire Chest and Highcrest Case all draw from all 194 pool-1 cards, and since RW3 with no map gate. So Pack 1 (on sale at Map 5) can give any of the 122 cards that belong to Maps 7+ (Pack 2/3 or later), including 14 volcanic (lava) cards.
mistakes.fix: Give each pack its own pool by the owner tiers (Maps 0-6 → Pack 1, 7-13 → Pack 2, 14-20 → Pack 3): set source.tier to 1 / 2 / 3 from the card's first map pool (the list below), and point SHOP_PACKS_DEFAULT pool at 1 / 2 / 3 (the base track and the skirmish drop read packCardPool too).

mistakes.what: 19 pack cards name a source map whose pack tier differs from where map-pools.json first puts them (a side map counts from the map that unlocks it, owner: "Submap cards are found in the Pack tier following the maps that unlock them").
mistakes.fix: Re-point source.map to the pool map (or move the card in map-pools.json), then re-tier.

mistakes.what: 39 live pack-pool cards are in no map pool and name no map, so they have no pack tier (the base track and drops treat them as Map 5, packs give them anywhere).
mistakes.fix: Place each in a map pool (canonical/map-pools.json) and give it source.map, or retire it.

mistakes.what: 53 live pack cards name a source map but are in no map pool (map-pools.json), so no fight of that map uses them.
mistakes.fix: Add them to their map's pool, or re-point source.map.

mistakes.what: 9 Hummingbird faction cards come "from the start" as Base (no source, unlocked), outside the faction pool.
mistakes.fix: Give them source {kind:pack, tier:11, side:tribes} (faction pool) unless they are the Hummingbird starter cards.

mistakes.what: Base (not tutorial) holds 10 cards; the owner's target is about 10 or fewer.
mistakes.fix: Move the non-starter Base cards with skills (and the Rare/Uncommon ones) to the faction pool, a skirmish reward or Pack 1; keep the plain Map 0 animals as Tutorial base.

mistakes.what: Outside the faction pool there are 3 Otter-type and 4 Hummingbird-type cards (owner 19:36: only 1-2 neutral otters and 1-2 traitor / neutral hummingbirds).
mistakes.fix: Keep 1-2 of each as named neutrals / traitors; move the rest into the faction pool (or rename them out of the faction).

mistakes.what: The faction pool holds your side + shared cards only (factionCardsOfMine); the owner's pool holds both sides ("that's how you would get the other faction's cards").
mistakes.fix: factionCardsOfMine: both sides + shared, the other side's cards weighted lower or later on the pattern.

mistakes.what: Pool copies per card are FACTION_POOL_COPIES {"common":5,"uncommon":4,"rare":3,"veryrare":2,"superrare":2}; the owner's rule is "pool size = the most duplicates you can hold in a deck" (RARITY_MAX_COPIES: common 5, uncommon 4, rare 3, very rare 2, super rare 1).
mistakes.fix: Read the copies from maxCopiesForRarity (Super Rare 2 → 1).

mistakes.what: No Base cards are added to the faction pool ("add 1 of each base card inside as well").
mistakes.fix: loadFactionPool: 1 copy of each Base card in the pool too.

mistakes.what: The standard faction reward is a weighted random draw behind rarity gates (FACTION_RARITY_GATES: 25 received for Uncommon, 40 + Map 14 for Rare ...), not the fixed C, C, C, U, C, C, U, C, U, R ... pattern.
mistakes.fix: A fixed pattern table (see the pacing check) and "set" vs "random" faction rewards as two hand-out kinds.

mistakes.what: All 11 Mystery Booster (pool 99) cards are unattainable, so the Mystery Booster / future Pack Secrets I pool is empty in play.
mistakes.fix: Clear `unattainable` on the ones ready, then make it the Pack Secrets I pool (a <1% slot in Packs 1-6).

mistakes.what: 3 cards outside Tutorial base start at Level 0 (Bee Knight, Forager Ant, Sparrow Chick: cardBaseLevel gives 0 to every basic / starter / quest / source-Base card), and since TU2 every new faction copy comes at Level 0; the owner: only the tutorial base units and the baby cards start at 0.
mistakes.fix: cardBaseLevel: 0 only for tutorial base (and babies); undo TU2's faction Level 0 copies.

mistakes.what: The advanced packs are "Advanced <pack>" (advancedPackOf); the owner calls them Collector packs.

The game calls faction:"base" cards and skirmish rewards "Base" (UT, 2026-10-19: "Base cards just mean they come from Skirmish rewards"); the owner now says Skirmish base for skirmish rewards and Base for the starting cards.
mistakes.fix: Rename the Codex sections and cardWhereToGetText lines.

facts: Egg items (EGG_KINDS, 7 kinds) drop from first clears (2-20% by fight kind), 0.1% per Energy on repeats, 1% from raids; Map 1's 1-3 and Map 3 each guarantee one. They sit in "🥚 Eggs in your pack" (the Nest picker's first section) until set in a nest; they hatch in 6-10 h into a random Common-Rare map or pack card of their type, at Level 0 (a "hatchling"), and the 🌱 Train section raises it to Level 1 for Kibble, Dust and Maple Leaves.

Egg cards (egg-woodland ... egg-beast) are different: a collection card given once when you first set that kind of egg in a nest (grantEggCardFor). They are playable (0 Attack, Wait 5-10) and crack open in battle into a random card of their type when Ready (engine hatchEggCard). They start at Level 1 and level like any card. They never show in the Nest's first section (that lists egg items and Level-0 cards).

Babies today are Nest items, not cards: a 6% "rescue" after any won Conquest fight (rollBabyRescue) gives a baby of the deck's main type; it grows in 4 h into a random card of that type at Level 0 (+2 Kibble), which the Nest then trains to Level 1.

The "baby" cards in the card list (Baby Bat, Baby Horned Capybara, Caiman Hatchling, Duckling, Otter Kit, Fox Kit, Rabbit Kit, Terrier Pup ...) are ordinary pack, skirmish or base cards: they do not hatch or change, start at Level 1 (pack) or 0 (base) and Forge to 10.
inconsistencies: Owner: babies drop like eggs, hatch / change into something else, and can never reach Level 1. Today no card behaves like that: the baby cards are normal cards that level to 10, and the Nest's "hatchlings" (Level 0 cards from eggs and rescued babies) are exactly what the Nest trains to Level 1.

Owner: "I don't see them in Raise or Hatch, the first section." Egg cards and baby cards never appear in the Nest picker: its first section lists egg ITEMS, its second only Level-0 copies. An egg card is Level 1 at once; a baby card is Level 1 (pack) or a base card at 0.
Owner: "you can play Eggs and babies". Egg cards: yes (they crack open in battle). Baby cards: yes, as ordinary units. Rescued babies and egg items: no (items).
Two of the egg-like cards are unattainable (Snapper Hatchling, Fire Drake Hatchling; the Red Dragon Egg is the Scale Trail quest's and unattainable), and Nest Hatchling has no source.
eggs.proposal: A "Baby" card kind (cardType baby): dropped like an egg (same rates), shown in the Nest's first section next to egg items, playable at Level 0, cannot be trained or Forged, and grows into a named card (hatchInto.defId) or a random card of its type after N hours in a nest. Rename the Nest's two sections "Hatch" (eggs and babies) and "Raise" (Level-0 tutorial base cards to Level 1).
